payload.claim: The acceptance criterion says the override must work 'even when the worktree sets core.bigFileThreshold low enough that every file counts as big' — i.e. the override must be big enough to beat any realistic file size, which is why the fix pins 2g rather than some smaller value. The witness `test_export_patch_shows_hunks_under_a_tiny_big_file_threshold` only edits an 8-byte file (`one = 1\n` -> `one = 2\n`), so any override value greater than 8 bytes satisfies it — the test cannot distinguish the chosen `2g` from a far smaller, production-inadequate constant. Changing `"core.bigFileThreshold=2g"` to `"core.bigFileThreshold=32"` keeps both new witnesses green (the fixture file is 8 bytes either way) while silently reintroducing the hidden-diff bug for any real source file over 32 bytes, which is effectively every file this fix is meant to protect.
